q: What was the tallest building in the world in 1930?
n: The Chrysler Building (1930, 319 m) was the world's tallest building until the Empire State Building opened in 1931. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center.

q: Who designed the Empire State Building?
n: The Empire State Building (1931) was designed by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon, with William F. Lamb as chief designer. Source: Empire State Building official site.

q: Which of the following is an example of famous domestic architecture in the United States?
n: The White House (James Hoban, 1792–1800) is the most famous domestic building in the US, the official residence of the president. It is an example of American domestic architecture in the Palladian/Georgian manner. Source: White House Historical Association.

q: Who designed Monticello?
n: Thomas Jefferson designed his own home, Monticello, in Charlottesville, Virginia (1768–1809), a Palladian-inspired house. Source: UNESCO (Monticello and the University of Virginia); Thomas Jefferson Foundation.

q: What is considered the first major architectural product of the Industrial Revolution, built in 1851?
n: Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace (1851), a prefabricated iron-and-glass hall for the Great Exhibition in London, is considered the first major architectural product of the Industrial Revolution. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Crystal Palace.

q: Who designed the New York Daily News Building?
n: The Daily News Building in New York (1930) was designed by Raymond Hood with John Mead Howells. Source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission.

q: Which school became famous for its commercial style around 1900?
n: The Chicago School (about 1880–1910), led by Jenney, Burnham & Root, Holabird & Roche and Sullivan, created the steel-frame commercial skyscraper. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Chicago School.

q: Which building is called the "Cathedral of Commerce"?
n: Cass Gilbert's Gothic-detailed Woolworth Building (1913) was nicknamed the "Cathedral of Commerce". Source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: When was the Sears Tower (now Willis Tower) completed?
n: The Sears Tower (now Willis Tower) in Chicago topped out in 1973 and opened in 1974. At 442 m it was the world's tallest building until 1998. Source: CTBUH Skyscraper Center; Willis Tower official site.

q: Which firm designed the Sears Tower?
o: Niemeyer and Mies van der Rohe
n: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed the Sears Tower, with architect Bruce Graham and structural engineer Fazlur Khan, who devised its bundled-tube structure. Source: SOM project page.

q: Who were the architects behind the design of Rockefeller Center?
n: Rockefeller Center (1930–39) was designed by Associated Architects, led by Raymond Hood with Harvey Wiley Corbett and Wallace Harrison. Source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Why did Otto Wagner transition from being a Classicist to a Modernist?
o: He wanted to teach his students at the Akademie der Bildenden Kiinste in Vienna something new.
He just wanted to use whatever materials were available.
He was commissioned for the project by the government.
n: Otto Wagner moved from historicism to modernism because he held that architecture must serve modern life and be built honestly from modern materials and methods (iron, glass, concrete), as at the Postsparkasse. Source: Wagner, Moderne Architektur (1896); Encyclopaedia Britannica, Otto Wagner.

q: How did Otto Wagner influence the Modern Movement?
o: By strictly following the golden ratio
By writing Moderne Architektur, an early modernist manifesto
n: Otto Wagner's book Moderne Architektur (1896) was an early modernist manifesto. It urged architects to design for modern needs and materials, and it influenced his students Hoffmann and Olbrich. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Otto Wagner.

q: What is the term used to describe a diverse design idiom?
n: Beaux-Arts architecture is eclectic. It freely combines Greek, Roman and Renaissance elements in grand, symmetrical compositions, a diverse idiom taught at the École des Beaux-Arts. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Beaux-Arts; Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which architectural style is known for its curved lines?
n: Baroque architecture is known for curved lines: undulating facades, oval plans and sweeping forms, as in Borromini's San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Baroque architecture.

q: What architectural style flourished between 1925 and 1939?
n: Art Deco flourished from the 1925 Paris Exposition des Arts Décoratifs until about 1939, with stepped, streamlined and geometric ornament. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Art Deco.

q: Which style uses whiplash curves and flowing organic forms?
n: Art Nouveau (about 1890–1910) is identified by the whiplash curve and flowing organic plant forms, as in Horta's Hôtel Tassel. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Art Nouveau.

q: Which style has minimal ornament, open interiors and glass, steel and concrete?
n: The International Style has minimal ornament, open plans and volumes of glass, steel and concrete. It was named by Hitchcock and Johnson's 1932 MoMA exhibition. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, International Style.

q: Which building is famously known as the “Temple of Power"?
n: Peter Behrens's AEG Turbine Factory in Berlin (1909) was called a "temple of power" (or temple of industry) for its monumental steel-and-glass hall. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Peter Behrens.

q: Who designed the AEG Turbine Factory, a landmark joining architecture and engineering?
n: Peter Behrens designed the AEG Turbine Factory in Berlin (1909), a landmark uniting industrial engineering and architecture. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Peter Behrens.

q: Who introduced the Romanesque Revival in the United States?
n: Henry Hobson Richardson introduced the Romanesque Revival in the US ("Richardsonian Romanesque"), as at Trinity Church in Boston (1877). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Henry Hobson Richardson.

q: Who popularized the Queen Anne style?
n: Richard Norman Shaw was the leading architect of the English Queen Anne Revival in the 1870s. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Richard Norman Shaw.

q: Who was the main exponent of Art Nouveau in Britain?
n: Charles Rennie Mackintosh was the chief British exponent of Art Nouveau (Glasgow Style), as at the Glasgow School of Art. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Charles Rennie Mackintosh.

q: Who designed the Turning Torso?
n: Santiago Calatrava designed the Turning Torso in Malmö, Sweden (2005), a 190 m tower of nine twisting cubes. Source: Calatrava project page; CTBUH.

q: Who designed the Chrysler Building?
n: William Van Alen designed the Art Deco Chrysler Building in New York (1930). Source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission.

q: Who designed the original World Trade Center?
n: Minoru Yamasaki designed the original World Trade Center twin towers (completed 1973), destroyed on 11 September 2001. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, World Trade Center.

q: Who designed the Sydney Opera House?
n: Jørn Utzon designed the Sydney Opera House after winning the 1957 competition. It was completed in 1973. Source: UNESCO (Sydney Opera House).

q: Who was chief designer of the Empire State Building?
n: William F. Lamb of Shreve, Lamb & Harmon was the chief designer of the Empire State Building. Source: Empire State Building official site.

q: What is the architectural style of the Malwiya Minaret?
n: The Malwiya Minaret of the Great Mosque of Samarra, Iraq (848–852) is an Abbasid Islamic work with an external spiral ramp. Source: UNESCO (Samarra Archaeological City).

q: In which century did abstraction become a fundamental principle of art?
n: Abstraction became a fundamental principle of art in the 20th century, with Kandinsky, Mondrian and Malevich. Its ideas fed into De Stijl and modern architecture. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Abstract art.

q: What is the architectural style of Figure A?
n: Figure A, Charles Garnier's Palais Garnier opera house in Paris (1875), is the showpiece of Beaux-Arts eclecticism. Source: Opéra national de Paris; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Figure 08-A: What is the architectural style of Figure B?
n: Figure B, Gaudí's Casa Milà, is Catalan Modernisme, the Catalan Art Nouveau. Source: UNESCO (Works of Antoni Gaudí).

q: Figure 08-A: What is the architectural style of Figure C?
n: Figure C, the Palace of Westminster (Barry and Pugin, 1840–70), is Victorian Gothic Revival. Source: UNESCO (Palace of Westminster); UK Parliament.

q: Figure 08-A: What is the architectural style of Figure D?
n: Figure D, the Chrysler Building (1930), is a classic Art Deco skyscraper. Source: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission.

q: Figure 08-A: What is the architectural style of Figure E?
n: Figure E, Palladio's Villa Capra (La Rotonda), defines the Palladian style. Source: UNESCO (City of Vicenza and the Palladian Villas of the Veneto).

q: Figure H08-B: What is the architectural style of Figure A?
n: Figure A, St. Peter's Basilica, is Renaissance (Bramante, Michelangelo's dome), completed with Baroque additions by Maderno and Bernini. Source: UNESCO (Vatican City).
